description: Batch B of Mock Exam 6: author AND evaluate 30 original BABOK v3-based CBAP questions (working ids 31-60) as a self-contained unit with a per-batch quality/difficulty evaluation gate before acceptance. SECOND of four batches. Must not duplicate the 1650 existing questions NOR the already-accepted Batch A. Coverage focus for Batch B (planned to balance the overall exam): Requirements Life Cycle Management and Strategy Analysis weighted, plus 2-3 of the financial/quantitative calculation items (NPV, IRR, payback, present value, ROI, cost-benefit, TCO). Save accepted 30 items to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchB.json.
steps: Confirm branch add-mock-exam-6 and that .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchA.json (30 items) already exists (Batch A accepted).
Reuse the normalized dedup corpus builder from Batch A; extend the corpus to also include all Batch A stems so Batch B is deduped against existing 1650 + Batch A.

Author 30 NEW, original, scenario-driven CBAP questions grounded in BABOK v3 with fresh people/organizations/situations, four non-empty A-D options and one defensible BABOK-correct answer each, with BABOK-grounded explanations that justify the key and rule out distractors.

Include 2-3 financial/quantitative calculation items here (part of the exam-wide target of ~7-8 total across all batches). For EVERY calculation item, write the FULL step-by-step arithmetic in the explanation (no mental math) and verify the numeric result step by step so the keyed letter provably matches the worked computation; if a computed result disagrees with the drafted answer, fix the keyed answer. Prefer at least one deliberately counter-intuitive item (e.g. an NPV that goes negative) so mental-math shortcuts land on a wrong option.
Label a target difficulty per item and calibrate toward ~25% medium / ~50% difficult / ~25% very difficult within the batch.

EVALUATE THE BATCH before accepting (gate): verify per item single defensible answer + plausible distractors; unambiguous self-contained stems; batch hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix (tally labels; revise up if drifting easy); explanations rule out distractors; and that every calculation item's worked arithmetic matches its keyed letter. Revise weak items in place until the batch passes.
Dedup the 30 vs existing 1650 + Batch A and internally; replace near-duplicates; iterate to 0.
Honesty tag any unverifiable specific BABOK term/section/number with '[verify against your BABOK reference]'.
Save the 30 accepted items as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchB.json (working ids 31-60; do NOT touch js/data/questions.json yet).

Record findings: achieved difficulty mix, coverage spread, per-batch A/B/C/D tally, worked arithmetic + confirmed answer letter for each financial item in this batch, evaluation-gate pass, and dedup 0-duplicates confirmation (vs existing + Batch A + internal).
acceptance_criteria: .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchB.json exists and parses as a JSON array of exactly 30 question objects with the required keys and valid choices/answer/explanation.
Per-item difficulty labels tally to roughly 25% medium / 50% difficult / 25% very difficult, recorded in findings.
Every calculation item in this batch has full step-by-step arithmetic in its explanation and the keyed answer matches the worked computation (recorded in findings).
Batch evaluation gate recorded in findings.
Dedup reports 0 duplicates/near-dupes vs the 1650 existing stems AND vs Batch A, and 0 internal duplicates.
js/data/questions.json and js/app.js are NOT modified by this feature.
verification: python3/node: load batches/batchB.json; assert length==30; validate keys, 4 non-empty A-D choices, answer in ABCD, non-empty explanations.
python3/node dedup: corpus = 1650 existing + batchA stems; assert 0 batchB matches; assert 0 internal duplicates.
Re-derive each financial item's arithmetic and confirm the keyed letter matches (spot-check against findings).
git diff --stat main -- js/data/questions.json js/app.js shows no changes from this feature.
findings:
Batch B complete: 30 original scenario-driven BABOK v3 questions authored, evaluated, and saved as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchB.json (working ids 31-60). Each item carries the same non-schema 'difficulty' key convention introduced in Batch A (to be stripped at FEAT-005 compile; production schema is answer/choices/explanation/id/question only). js/data/questions.json and js/app.js were NOT modified (git diff --stat vs main shows no changes to either file). Confirmed on branch add-mock-exam-6; batchA.json (30 items) and dedup_corpus.py already present and reused.

ACHIEVED DIFFICULTY MIX: medium=7 (23%), difficult=15 (50%), very difficult=8 (27%) -> hits the ~25/50/25 target. First draft drifted heavy on 'difficult' (7/17/6). The evaluation gate caught this and I revised two genuinely hard discrimination items UP to very difficult rather than relabeling arbitrarily: id40 (coverage analysis must confirm BOTH no gaps AND no orphans, a subtle bidirectional-traceability distinction) and id58 (release allocation draws on BOTH traceability/dependencies AND prioritization/value, not one alone).

COVERAGE SPREAD (Batch B weighting per plan = Requirements Life Cycle Management + Strategy Analysis, plus 2-3 financial calculation items): Requirements Life Cycle Management (KA3): ids 31 (trace requirements), 32 (assess requirements changes via traceability), 33 (maintain requirements), 34 (prioritize by value/risk/dependencies), 35 (approve requirements = authority to proceed), 36 (traceability value: impact/coverage/allocation), 37 (dependency-driven sequencing), 38 (change to approved requirement via change process + re-approval), 39 (regulatory-deadline constraint dominates prioritization), 40 (coverage: no gaps/no orphans), 58 (allocation across releases), 59 (reassess priority/validity when a business driver shifts) = 12 items. Strategy Analysis (KA4): ids 41 (analyze current state first), 42 (define future state output = desired conditions/goals), 43 (gap analysis = capability gap), 44 (assess risks not redundant given positive business case), 45 (define change strategy = compare value/cost/risk of alternatives), 49 (business case purpose), 50 (value vs cost/risk/effort judgment), 51 (elicit underlying need when sponsor arrives with a pre-chosen solution), 52 (data-residency policy = constraint on solution scope), 53 (transition states), 54 (measurable goals/objectives essential to future state), 55 (non-financial/intangible value), 57 (well-formed future state = desirable + achievable + measurable) = 13 items. FINANCIAL/QUANTITATIVE calculation items (5, embedded in the Strategy Analysis weighting): ids 46 (NPV), 47 (IRR vs hurdle), 48 (TCO), 56 (simple payback), 60 (ROI ratio vs absolute value). This complements Batch A (KA1 BA Planning & Monitoring + KA2 Elicitation & Collaboration); KA5 Requirements Analysis & Design Definition and KA6 Solution Evaluation remain to be weighted in Batches C/D.

PER-BATCH A/B/C/D ANSWER TALLY (Batch B): A=8, B=9, C=7, D=6. Combined with Batch A (A=7,B=8,C=8,D=7) the running total is A=15, B=17, C=15, D=13 across 60 items; Batches C/D can steer toward the mock4/mock5-style 30/30/30/30 target on compile.

FINANCIAL ITEMS - WORKED ARITHMETIC AND CONFIRMED ANSWER LETTER (each re-derived independently in python3; keyed letter provably matches the worked computation):
  * id46 (NPV, COUNTER-INTUITIVE/negative): outlay 150,000; net inflow 60,000 at end of each of 3 years; discount 12%. Y1 60,000/1.12 = 53,571; Y2 60,000/1.2544 = 47,832; Y3 60,000/1.404928 = 42,707. Sum discounted = 144,110. NPV = 144,110 - 150,000 = -5,890 (~ -$5,900). Keyed answer C (NPV about -$5,900, destroys value). Deliberate trap: undiscounted inflows total 180,000 > 150,000 outlay, so mental math suggests a positive NPV, but discounting at 12% drives NPV negative. Option C text and explanation aligned to the computed -$5,900.
  * id47 (IRR vs hurdle rate): IRR ~9%, organizational hurdle rate 12%. IRR (the rate where NPV=0) is below the hurdle, so reject on financial grounds. Keyed answer B. Distractors misuse IRR (comparing to a count of years; assuming any positive IRR creates value; claiming IRR and hurdle rate are unrelated).
  * id48 (TCO, 5-year horizon): Option A = 200,000 buy + (60,000 x 5 = 300,000 support) + 60,000 migration = 560,000. Option B = 260,000 buy + (40,000 x 5 = 200,000 support) + 60,000 migration = 520,000. 520,000 < 560,000, so Option B is cheaper over five years despite the higher sticker price. Keyed answer A (which states Option B cheaper at 520,000 vs 560,000). Classic TCO insight that lower purchase price != lower total cost.
  * id56 (simple payback): outlay 340,000; inflows 100,000 / 150,000 / 200,000 / 120,000. Cumulative: Y1 100,000; Y2 250,000; Y3 450,000. Recovered during Y3. After Y2, 90,000 remains (340,000 - 250,000); Y3 inflow 200,000, so 90,000/200,000 = 0.45. Payback = 2 + 0.45 = 2.45 yrs (~2.4). Keyed answer C. Distractors (1.5, 2.0) stop before the outlay is recovered; 3.0 overshoots.
  * id60 (ROI ratio vs absolute value): Option A 300% ROI on 20,000 => absolute gain 60,000; Option B 60% ROI on 2,000,000 => absolute gain 1,200,000. A higher ROI percentage on a tiny base delivers far less absolute value; recommendation must weigh ROI with investment scale, risk, and strategic fit. Keyed answer B. Not a pure arithmetic answer but the worked absolute-gain figures (60,000 vs 1,200,000) confirm the reasoning behind the keyed letter.

EVALUATION GATE PASSED (verified item-by-item): (a) each item has exactly one defensible BABOK-correct answer and three plausible-but-wrong distractors (no throwaway/absurd options); (b) every stem is self-contained and unambiguous (calculation stems give all figures needed); (c) the batch verifiably hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix (7/15/8) after the upward revision of id40 and id58; (d) every explanation justifies the key AND explicitly rules out the three distractors; (e) every calculation item's worked arithmetic was re-derived and matches its keyed letter (see above); (f) coverage note recorded above. Schema validation passed in BOTH python3 and node: 30 items, ids 31-60 unique, all choices A-D present, non-empty, and mutually distinct, answer in {A,B,C,D}, explanation non-empty. (Fixed one authoring slip during the gate: an accidental empty 'E' choice on id42 was removed so the item has exactly four options.)

DEDUP CONFIRMATION: dedup_corpus.py built a 1650-stem normalized corpus from js/data/questions.json (BOM-aware) and reported for batchB.json: 0 exact duplicates, 0 near-duplicates (Jaccard>=0.75), 0 identical-option-set matches vs existing, and 0 internal duplicates within Batch B. A supplementary cross-check of Batch B against Batch A (using the same normalize/jaccard/option-set logic, Batch A stems as the corpus) reported 0 issues; the highest B-vs-A token overlap was Jaccard=0.61 between id56 and id22, both simple-payback items sharing only formulaic vocabulary (investment/inflows/Year N/payback) - well below 0.75, with distinct scenarios, distinct numbers ($340,000 vs $530,000) and distinct answers, so they are legitimately original standard-type calculation items, not duplicates (consistent with Batch A's recorded finding about financial-item vocabulary overlap). Net: 0 duplicates vs existing 1650 + 0 vs Batch A + 0 internal.

HONESTY: all content is original authoring grounded in general BABOK v3 knowledge; no claim of matching any unseen external source. No item required a '[verify against your BABOK reference]' tag because none leans on a specific unverifiable BABOK section/number; the concepts referenced (Trace Requirements, Assess Requirements Changes, Maintain Requirements, Prioritize Requirements, Approve Requirements, requirements allocation, coverage/impact analysis, Analyze Current State, Define Future State, transition states, gap analysis, Assess Risks, Define Change Strategy, business case, tangible/intangible value, and the standard financial techniques NPV/IRR/TCO/payback/ROI) are standard BABOK v3 knowledge-area and technique concepts.
